solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: With pawn advantage, almost square?

parts.note: P is the chess notation abbreviation for a pawn

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: an asset is something that gives an advantage

explanation.surface: A chess player wonders whether being a pawn up leaves the position roughly level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' is not a geometric or chess term here but the slang for someone out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: Square as slang means old-fashioned and unhip, and a passé thing has gone out of fashion.

clue.text: The Ring slumping, but for end of Tristan and Isolde, initially animated

indicators.note: animated means the letters are set in lively motion and rearranged
but for says one letter is exchanged for another in the word slumping
end of picks the final letter of Tristan
initially picks the first letter of Isolde

explanation.surface: Wagner's Ring cycle sags, but Tristan and Isolde, initially at least, is lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Ring' is boxing, not Wagner. 'but for' swaps the N of SLUMPING for I, giving SLUMPIIG, which 'animated' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxing takes place in a ring, and the sport is often called the ring.

clue.text: Fishy plate mostly cut off bit of seafood

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a scale is one of the plates covering a fish
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A chef trims a fish dish, cutting off part of the seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallop is a bivalve shellfish, one item among the seafood on a menu.

clue.text: Large-scale cooking instructions, less about trussing

indicators.note: trussing in the sense of stringing up, so in a down clue the letters read upwards
less means those letters are taken away

parts.note: a recipe gives cooking instructions
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Recipe directions for something big, minus the bit about tying up the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' drops RE from RECIPE to leave CIPE; 'trussing', as stringing up, reverses it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is grand in scale or scope, like an epic journey.

clue.text: Vicar forgetting verse and CE'll change what their job is?

indicators.note: change tells us the pooled letters are rearranged into a new order
forgetting means leaving out a letter from the word Vicar

parts.note: the letters are used as printed, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A vicar and the Church of England will reform the way clergy duties are carried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' drops V from VICAR to leave ICAR; 'change' rearranges ICAR with CELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar's work is that of the clergy; the adjective describes anything belonging to churchmen or to office-type paperwork.

clue.text: Outlying island shifted, with line for sierra in north-south alignment?

indicators.note: shifted means the letters are moved around into a new order
for says one letter stands in place of another in the phrase

parts.note: Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A remote island has moved, with a line drawn replacing the mountains, in a north-south direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the S of OUTLYING ISLAND for L, and 'shifted' rearranges the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of longitude run from pole to pole, so something aligned that way runs north to south.

clue.text: Somewhat bloody runs before and during A&E

indicators.note: before puts the letter ahead of the rest

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: during puts the same letter in the middle of the pair

parts.note: the letters are taken as written, ignoring the ampersand

explanation.surface: Things look somewhat bloody as someone rushes to and through Accident and Emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: One R for 'runs' is used twice, once 'before' and once 'during' A&E, the hospital casualty department.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare steak is lightly cooked and still red and bloody inside.

clue.text: Comic actor's place in linked series

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a chain is a series of linked items

explanation.surface: A comedian's position in a sequence of connected items.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin was the silent-film comedian and actor.

clue.text: First of dark fruits put as far down as possible in loamy soil

indicators.note: first of names the opening letter of those fruits as the one to shift

indicators.text: put as far down as possible
indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the end, so the letter moves to the very end

parts.note: sloes are small dark blackthorn fruits

explanation.surface: Plant dark berries as deep as you can in good soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of SLOES goes to the bottom of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Loess is a fine wind-blown silt that forms fertile loam-like soil.

clue.text: Cape money is invested in jewel to stop representative making a big deal?

indicators.note: to stop means to plug, so the piece fills the gap in another

parts.note: an agent is a representative

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, as money is put into something

parts.note: a gem is a jewel
the rand is the currency of South Africa, home of the Cape

explanation.surface: South African money is sunk into a jewel to keep an agent quiet, making a big fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape money' points to South Africa's currency; 'to stop' means plug a gap, so the jewel-and-money piece fills the middle of the representative.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggrandisement is making something greater, so literally making something or someone big.

clue.text: Nibbling on part of flying insect? There's not tons

indicators.note: there's not says one letter is absent from the phrase

parts.note: a gnat's wing is one part of a small flying insect

explanation.surface: Something is chewing on a bit of an insect's anatomy, though not in any great quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's not' removes the T from GNAT WING.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnawing is biting away at something persistently, just as nibbling is taking small repeated bites.

clue.text: Code for changing some low aria to cued run that transposes William Tell

wordplay.reading: WILLIAM put through the code that turns SOME LOW ARIA into CUED RUN THAT

parts.words: Code for changing some low aria to cued run that transposes William
parts.note: matching the two phrases letter by letter gives a substitution cipher: S becomes C, O becomes U, M becomes E, E becomes D, L becomes R, W becomes N, A becomes T, R becomes H, I becomes A; applying it to the letters of William gives the answer

explanation.surface: Some kind of cipher garbles a dull operatic aria, much as Rossini's William Tell overture is famously reworked.
explanation.walkthrough: Line up SOME LOW ARIA over CUED RUN THAT: each letter maps to the one below. Encode W-I-L-L-I-A-M: W to N, I to A, L to R, L to R, I to A, A to T, M to E.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell a story is to recount it, which is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Compose composer's missing finale

indicators.note: missing finale says the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Jean-Baptiste Lully was a French Baroque composer; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: An instruction to write music, noting that a composer has left his work without an ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compose' is the verb meaning calm, not write music; Lully is the French Baroque composer.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose someone is to calm or soothe them, and to lull is to soothe into quiet.

clue.text: Piece of furniture I constructed of waste material

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone says they built a bit of furniture themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is the chief nitrogenous waste in urine, so the adjective relates to waste excreted by the body.

clue.text: Adverts overlooking grand advantage

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so that letter is left out

parts.note: plugs are promotional mentions, a kind of advert
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Advertising that ignores a big spender still has its benefits.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is a positive point or benefit, the same as an advantage.

clue.text: Set up dark style of film with second part for Holly Hunter

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: film noir is a dark, moody style of cinema

indicators.note: second part picks the second letter of Holly

explanation.surface: A dark film is arranged with a supporting role for the actress Holly Hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holly Hunter' looks like the actress; Holly gives its second letter and Hunter is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is the great hunter of Greek myth, also a constellation.

clue.text: Places reference facing up, way off stockpile

indicators.note: facing up in a down clue means the letters read upwards
off means those letters are removed

parts.note: to salt away is to stockpile or hoard
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reference books are lined up while a stockpile is set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' takes WAY from SALT AWAY, leaving SALTA; 'facing up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps, a reference work for looking up places.

clue.text: Pensioning almost yearly breaks ruined US giant

indicators.note: breaks says one piece splits the other open
ruined means the letters of US giant are wrecked and reassembled
almost means the last letter of the phrase is lost

parts.note: per annum is the Latin phrase meaning yearly

explanation.surface: An American giant collapses, with annual holidays almost wrecking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' turns US GIANT into USATING; PERANNU breaks into it after US.
explanation.definitionFit: To superannuate is to retire someone on a pension, so the participle means pensioning off.

clue.text: I'm asking to come in, taking time out for endless oddity

indicators.note: taking signals that one letter of the word is replaced
out for says the letter leaves and something takes its place

parts.note: to enter is to come in

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a quirk is an oddity

explanation.surface: A visitor requests entry, pausing to swap time for a little eccentricity.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of ENTER is replaced by QUIR. 'I'm asking' defines the person who asks.
explanation.definitionFit: An enquirer is one who asks questions, so the clue speaks in that person's voice.

clue.text: Head monk with computer work takes place in early afternoon of getting in order

parts.note: a prior is the head of a priory of monks
IT, information technology, is computer work
an event that takes place at one o'clock 'is at I', I being the Roman numeral one
on can replace of, as in a book on or of a subject

explanation.surface: A senior monk does some computing during the early afternoon before tidying things up.
explanation.walkthrough: IS AT I reads as 'is at one (pm)', I being one in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Prioritisation is the business of ranking tasks by importance, so it is the act of arranging things in sequence.

clue.text: Distribute otherwise genuine collection

parts.note: real means genuine
a lot is a collection, as at auction

explanation.surface: Share out a true collection in a different way.
explanation.definitionFit: To reallot is to assign shares again, handing them out differently.

clue.text: Maybe Lennon and Shankar losing their heads over European hero

indicators.note: over means the letters are turned round
losing their heads means each name drops its first letter

parts.note: John Lennon of the Beatles and Ravi Shankar the sitar player give two first names, John and Ravi

explanation.surface: Two famous musicians lose their heads over a European hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing their heads' turns JOHN RAVI into OHN AVI, and 'over' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivanhoe is the knightly hero of Walter Scott's novel of that name.

clue.text: Church version of bible, not one for high culture?

parts.note: AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A churchgoer's chosen Bible translation, perhaps judged too lowbrow for refined tastes.
explanation.walkthrough: A chav is British slang for a brash, loutish young person, stereotyped as uncultured.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang term names a supposedly vulgar youth, someone stereotypically indifferent to opera or fine art.

clue.text: Commanding officer mixed martial arts item seen in lists

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer; that the answer also sits at the start of Commanding is a coincidence

explanation.surface: An officer in charge is caught up in cage-fighting, featuring in fight rosters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lists' are written lists, not jousting lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Punctuation marks separating the items of a list are typically this mark.

clue.text: He flourished around period away from domesticity

indicators.note: around says one piece goes about the other

parts.note: fl. is the Latin abbreviation floruit, meaning he flourished, used in dating historical figures
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A man did well for a time once he was away from home life.
explanation.definitionFit: A feral animal has escaped domestication and lives wild, away from tame household life.

clue.text: Not allowed to touch when cycling

indicators.note: cycling means a letter is moved round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: to abut is to touch or border

explanation.surface: A rule bans touching anything while riding a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cycling' moves the T of ABUT from the end to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, meaning forbidden or prohibited.

clue.text: Till distant month

parts.note: far means distant

explanation.surface: Up to a far-off time of month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Till' is the verb meaning cultivate, not 'until'.
explanation.definitionFit: To till land is to plough and cultivate it, which is to work it agriculturally.

clue.text: Send up blood products, being for war?

indicators.note: send up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: sera are the clear fluids separated from blood

explanation.surface: Blood supplies are sent up to the front for a war effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a noun: a divine being, the Greek god of war.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares is the Greek god of war, a divine being responsible for battle.

clue.text: Sharp tool twisted into horse for Trojan's delivery?

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: twisted means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: an awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes

explanation.surface: A sharp tool is concealed inside a horse, like the Trojan Horse delivering soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: A Trojan is also a malicious program disguised as harmless software, so it delivers harmful code.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trojan in computing is a disguised program that brings harmful software onto a machine.

clue.text: Both political wings clutching primitive form of revolutionary cross?

indicators.note: clutching says the outer piece holds the others

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right
ur- is a prefix for the primitive or original form of something
Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: Left and right alike are hanging on to an early version of an angry revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' is not angry: a lurcher is a crossbred dog, usually greyhound with collie or terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog is by definition a crossbreed, so it is one example of a cross.

clue.text: Mechanically produce wordplay for 'carpal'?

definitions.meaning: to make something run by machine rather than by hand
split four and four, the answer is a word for car followed by a word for pal, so it is a clue that would build the quoted word

explanation.surface: A cheeky request for a clue to a wrist-bone word.
explanation.walkthrough: Carpal is the wrist bone; read it as CAR + PAL and the answer supplies the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To automate a process is to make it run by machine, producing things mechanically.

clue.text: Promise suits etc to dismiss men

indicators.note: to dismiss means those letters are sent away from the word

parts.note: menswear covers suits and other clothing for men
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tailor vows that suits and the like will be used to sack some staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to vow or give one's solemn word, the verb sense of promise.
